Approved for Unlimited Release as SAND2009-4307C Overview • Outline – Interdependence among Threat, Vulnerability and Consequence – Methodology overview – Example applications • Objective – Facilitate collaborative interdisciplinary security risk assessment – Enable security risks for one facility to be placed in the context of the wider security environment – Help decision makers decide which scenarios to mitigate at a specific facility INMM(TRAM) 7/15/09 2 Risk Defined • Risk is the potential for realization of adverse consequences. • Risk can be thought as answers to 3 questions: – What can happen? (scenario) – How likely is it? (probability / frequency) – How bad is it? (consequence) Many security risk assessment methods treat Threat, Vulnerability and Consequence as though they are quasi-independent. (At best, they are treated as conditional variables.)
